newsitem.title: UK: UK longer leading index up 0.1% in August.
newsitem.headline: UK longer leading index up 0.1% in August.

text.p: The Office for National Statistics released the following indices on economic activity in Britain:

NOTES - longer leader signals turning points in the economy some 13 months in advance, shorter leading index indicates turning points about five months in advance, coincident index moves in line with business cycle, lagging index shows turning points about 12 months after it happened.
The ONS said the longer index rose only slightly in August having risen steadily since December.
Higher housing starts just outweighed falling contributions from interest rates and the yield curve. The housing component turned positive for the first time since July 1995.
The ONS said the shorter leading index rose sharply due to increases in EC/GfK consumer confidence and share prices which outweighed a fall in seasonally adjusted new car registrations.

The coincident index rose in the three months to August due to continued growth in the contribution from retail sales and M0 real money supply. Their growth outweighed a fall in the index of production in July and continued falls in June and July in the contribution from CBI capacity utilisation, the ONS said.
